name: rotor-transition
note: THE TILTWING BLEND SIGN TEST - the highest-risk thing v1.0.0 shipped. ChaseController.cs:1128 carries a standing 'ponytail:' comment on the tilt-driven regime blend: tiltFrac = clamp01((GetWingAngle() - lo) / (hi - lo)), which ASSUMES maxAngle = engines-up = hover, i.e. tiltFrac 1 in the hover. The orientation is UNCONFIRMED and the branch was dead for 40 versions (the v0.58 helo probe never resolved - R39-rotor 1a), so nothing has ever tested it. The comment names the one-line fix: flip to (hi - angle) / (hi - lo) at :1132. READ THE ARITHMETIC BEFORE THE PASS CRITERION, because the obvious one is wrong. The blend is _heliBlend = MAX(speedRamp, tiltFrac), speedRamp = clamp01((HeliForwardSpeed - vFwd) / (HeliForwardSpeed - HeliHoverSpeed)). A max() CANNOT FALL as the aircraft slows, whatever the sign is, so 'heliBlend falls as speed falls' is not a reachable failure mode. What an inverted sign produces is heliBlend PINNED AT 1.0 FROM THE FIRST SAMPLE, at 140 m/s in wing-borne cruise, where the speed ramp is 0.000 and a correctly-signed tiltFrac must also be ~0. PASS: heliBlend is 0.000 on every row above HeliForwardSpeed and then rises monotonically to 1.000 as vFwd falls toward HeliHoverSpeed - i.e. it tracks the speed ramp exactly, and the residual heliBlend - clamp01((HeliForwardSpeed - vFwd)/(HeliForwardSpeed - HeliHoverSpeed)) stays ~0 throughout. Take HeliForwardSpeed and HeliHoverSpeed off the capture's OWN '# config' line: the shipped defaults are 60 and 20 since v0.58, but a persisted cfg may still hold the v0.43 150/40 that R39 flew, and the residual is meaningless against the wrong pair. FAIL: that residual is ~1.0 at the 140 m/s entry - the aircraft is flying wing-borne with the law told it is in a hover, which deletes the entire bank-to-turn demand (tBankE *= (1 - heliBlend)) and boosts yaw by HeliYawScale. NOT EXPOSED, and check this FIRST: if the spawn's '[helofbw]' line reads tiltwing=0 then TiltWingController did not resolve, the tilt term never ran, heliBlend is the speed ramp by construction, and a clean residual proves nothing. tiltwing=1 is the precondition for reading anything else. WHY QuadVTOL1 ALONE: it is the only tiltwing on the roster. AttackHelo1 cannot fly the card at all (Vmax 100 m/s) and UtilityHelo1 is a compound helo with no TiltWingController, so neither exercises the branch - and the control here is WITHIN the lane (the speed-ramp residual), which is stronger than a second airframe and costs no entry speed. ENTRY 140 m/s: 0.95 x Vmax is 141.2, so this is the fastest entry TestDrone.EntrySpeedFlyable will pass, deliberately as far above HeliForwardSpeed as the envelope allows so the speed ramp is unambiguously 0 at t=0. No startSpeedCorner - AIRFRAMES.md has no measured FBW corner for this airframe, so the multiple would fail soft to the absolute anyway. THROTTLE 0.25 IS THE DECELERATION: MinThrottle is 0.25 and EntryThrottle snaps anything lower back to the 0.70 DEFAULT, so this is the floor, not a preference. 70 s is sized to sweep the whole band rather than to a clock - if the aircraft has not reached HeliHoverSpeed by the end the test still works, because the readout is heliBlend against vFwd, never against t. az 10 deg is a constant marker offset held for the whole leg, inside the measured 11 deg pedal-saturation knee, so the turn channel is excited but unsaturated and the bank-to-yaw hand-off shows as error re-growth mid-sweep. Secondary read, from R39-rotor 6.4: bank and outY hand over monotonically with no sign reversals in outR, and 'off' stays under 3 deg throughout. SCORING GAP, stated because it is a real limit of this tag: scorecard.py's 'transition' arm computes altExcursionM plus the generic pointing/saturation block ONLY - it does not call wobble_scan, so there is no stickFlipRateR on this segment. Use flightscore.py --levers (xfightPct) for the roll/yaw cross-fight and analyze-wobble.py directly on the CSV for the hand-off transient. startAlt 3000: throttle 0.25 in wing-borne flight buys the deceleration with altitude, and this is a single-lane card, so at the Drone/DroneAltDeckM 3000 default it draws the LOW deck at 1500 m - still 1000 m above the floor, so a forgotten knob costs margin rather than the run. Set the knob to 0 anyway. count 2 over a 1-key list = TWO QuadVTOL1 LANES, wrapping, at zero wall-clock cost because lanes fly concurrently. This is the only card in the queue whose entire question lives on ONE airframe, and task #85 kills a lane outright: R40 lost 1 lane in 10 to a placement velocity blow-up ('aircraft gone' is FATAL and takes the remaining replicates with it). With one lane that is the whole test gone in an unattended night; with two it is half the replicates. R42 VERDICT (v1.0.1, shipped 60/20): THE CARD WORKED AND IT FAILED ITS OWN PASS CRITERION -- read LAW-LEDGER.md X30 before touching ChaseController.cs:1132. With HeliForwardSpeed reset to 60 the whole leg flies above it (min vFwd >= 60 m/s over 8 captures x 8960 rows), so speedRamp is identically 0.000 and heliBlend IS tiltFrac -- exactly the direct readout this card was designed to be and could not be in R41. Measured tiltFrac by 10 m/s bin: 0.620 (100-110), 0.535 (90-100), 0.377 (80-90), 0.224 (70-80), 0.182 (60-70). Time runs high-speed -> low-speed, so tiltFrac FALLS as the aircraft decelerates toward the hover; a correctly-oriented tiltFrac (1 = hover) must RISE. The card's PASS bar was 'heliBlend 0.000 on every row above HeliForwardSpeed' and it reads 0.18-0.62. Corroborated inside R41's own data: R41's heliBlend-minus-speedRamp residual is +0.002 in the three slow bins and +0.190 at 100-110 m/s, i.e. tiltFrac ~ 0.619 there, agreeing with R42's 0.620 to 0.001 -- the signal was always present, hidden under the max(). DO NOT SHIP THE ONE-LINE FLIP ON THIS ALONE: flipped, tiltFrac reads 0.380 at 108 m/s in wing-borne cruise where it must be ~0, so the measured 0.18-0.62 range fits NEITHER orientation and the defect may be the (lo, hi) limits rather than the sign. tiltwing=1 is confirmed in LogOutput.log, so the term did resolve. WHAT TO FLY NEXT (ledger O13): extend this card below HeliHoverSpeed. Throttle 0.25 is MinThrottle and the deceleration stalled at 60 m/s in R41 AND R42, so heliBlend in [0.75, 1.0] still has zero samples in the entire corpus. Pointing scores are unchanged R41->R42 (terminal 0.0471 vs 0.0641, rms 1.2418 vs 1.2417) and that is a COINCIDENCE, not stability: speedRamp at 150/40 happened to land within 0.002 of tiltFrac over the bulk of the leg.
